RU-C1-01-001.notes: чуть не + perfective past means 'almost' happened, though it didn't: чуть не упал. The не isn't a real negation, so the meaning is positive-but-averted. едва не is a more bookish synonym.

RU-C1-01-002.notes: Не успел я + perfective infinitive, как… means 'I'd barely … when…'. The inverted order (успел я) is typical of the construction, and the perfective войти marks a single completed act.

RU-C1-01-003.notes: Стоит только + perfective infinitive, как… means 'you only have to … and…'. The perfective сказать stresses a single act that triggers the reaction, and the main clause is in the present.

RU-C1-01-004.notes: The perfective future can describe typical, repeated behaviour, often with иногда or бывало: придёт и молчит. It presents each occurrence as a whole event, like English 'he'll come round'.

RU-C1-01-005.notes: Не буду делать (imperfective) is a flat refusal: I won't do it at all. Не сделаю (perfective) means I won't manage to get it done. Aspect turns refusal into inability.

RU-C1-01-006.notes: за- marks the start of an action: заплакать (burst into tears). вдруг (suddenly) often goes with these inceptive verbs. Likewise засмеяться, заговорить.

RU-C1-01-007.notes: по- + an activity verb gives a perfective meaning 'for a while': поработал. немного reinforces the limited duration. Likewise почитать, погулять.

RU-C1-01-008.notes: про- + a duration means spending the whole period doing something: проспал всю ночь. The same prefix also gives проспать in the sense 'oversleep'.

RU-C1-01-009.notes: на- + a verb with the genitive means doing something in large quantity: наготовила еды. The object goes into the genitive of quantity.

RU-C1-01-010.notes: пере- means doing something to excess: переесть (overeat). Likewise переутомиться, перестараться. The past переел keeps the irregular ел of есть.

RU-C1-01-011.notes: раз- + -ся marks an action that gets going and intensifies: разговориться (get talking). The cue tells you the group is mixed, so the plural -лись.

RU-C1-02-001.notes: принять решение is the standard collocation for 'take a decision'. сделать решение is a calque from English and is wrong. The imperfective is принимать решение.
RU-C1-02-001.tip: сделать решение is a calque; the collocation is принять решение.

RU-C1-02-002.notes: оказать помощь + dative is the formal collocation for 'give help'. In speech, помочь is used. пострадавшим is a participle used as a noun: the injured.

RU-C1-02-003.notes: провести исследование means 'carry out a study'. провести also collocates with опрос (survey), встречу (meeting) and время (spend time).

RU-C1-02-004.notes: произвести впечатление на + accusative means 'make an impression on'. The past произвёл has ё and no -л-, like вёл.

RU-C1-02-005.notes: принять участие в + prepositional means 'take part in'. It's the formal equivalent of участвовать в.

RU-C1-02-006.notes: обратить внимание на + accusative means 'pay attention to, note'. Обратите внимание is common in instructions and lectures.

RU-C1-02-007.notes: осуществлять контроль за / над + instrumental is officialese for 'oversee'. Such verb + noun phrases are typical of bureaucratic style.

RU-C1-02-008.notes: внести предложение means 'put forward a proposal' in parliamentary language. внёс keeps the irregular past of нести.

RU-C1-03-001.notes: по + prepositional of a verbal noun means 'upon': по окончании (upon completion). The ending is -и, not -ю: по окончанию is a common error.

RU-C1-03-002.notes: по приезде (upon arrival) is an old prepositional form in -е. по приезду is widespread but non-standard.

RU-C1-03-003.notes: согласно takes the dative: согласно закону. The genitive (согласно закона) is a common error in official texts.

RU-C1-03-004.notes: вопреки + dative means 'contrary to, in defiance of': вопреки совету. It's stronger than несмотря на.

RU-C1-03-005.notes: ввиду + genitive means 'in view of' and is written as one word. в виду (in sight) is a different phrase: иметь в виду (bear in mind).

RU-C1-03-006.notes: в ходе + genitive means 'in the course of': в ходе переговоров. It's typical of news reports. The phrase в ходе дела means 'in the course of business'.

RU-C1-03-007.notes: в рамках + genitive means 'within the framework of, as part of'. It's frequent in official and business Russian.

RU-C1-03-008.notes: по мере + genitive means 'as something progresses': по мере развития. With a clause it's по мере того как.

RU-C1-03-009.notes: на основании + genitive means 'on the basis of'. данные (data) is plural in Russian, like English 'these data'.

RU-C1-03-010.notes: в целях + genitive means 'for the purpose of': в целях безопасности. It's typical of official notices.

RU-C1-03-011.notes: в силу + genitive means 'owing to, by virtue of'. в силу обстоятельств (owing to circumstances) is a set phrase.

RU-C1-04-001.notes: интерес takes к + dative: интерес к истории. The verb интересоваться takes the instrumental instead, so noun and verb differ.

RU-C1-04-002.notes: относиться к + dative asks for an opinion or attitude. The noun отношение takes к as well: отношение к искусству.
RU-C1-04-002.tr: What do you think of contemporary art?
RU-C1-04-002.flag: dup: replaced Как вы относитесь к этому? (near-identical to B1 Как ты относишься к этому?)

RU-C1-04-003.notes: уверен в + prepositional means 'confident of': уверен в успехе. With a clause it's уверен, что. The noun уверенность also takes в: уверенность в себе (self-confidence).

RU-C1-04-004.notes: участие takes в + prepositional, like the verb участвовать: участие в жизни города. активное участие is a common collocation.
RU-C1-04-004.text: Она принимает активное участие {{c1::в::preposition (участие …)}} жизни города.
RU-C1-04-004.tr: She plays an active part in the life of the city.
RU-C1-04-004.flag: dup: replaced Он принял участие в конкурсе (near-identical to C1-02-005)

RU-C1-04-005.notes: победа takes над + instrumental: победа над соперником. одержать победу is the formal collocation for 'win'.

RU-C1-04-006.notes: ответ takes на + accusative, like the verb ответить на: ответ на письмо. The person answered goes in the dative.

RU-C1-04-007.notes: надежда takes на + accusative, like надеяться на: надежда на улучшение. The verb надеяться on its own takes на as well.

RU-C1-04-008.notes: причина takes the genitive: причина аварии. The preposition для is not used here. The noun повод (occasion, pretext) takes для: повод для радости.

RU-C1-04-009.notes: любовь takes к + dative: любовь к детям. из любви means 'out of love', with из + genitive of motive.

RU-C1-04-010.notes: контроль takes над + instrumental for power over something: контроль над ситуацией. контроль за + instrumental means supervision.

RU-C1-05-001.notes: Perfective verbal adverbs from -йти verbs end in -я, not -в: придя. прийдя is a common misspelling. The imperfective counterpart, приходя, means 'while coming'.

RU-C1-05-002.notes: войти gives войдя, with -я. The action is completed before the main verb (включила). Its imperfective, входя, means 'on entering, as one enters'.

RU-C1-05-003.notes: найти gives найдя. The form найдя is perfective, though it looks like an imperfective -я form. The past active participle, нашедший, is formed from the stem наш-.

RU-C1-05-004.notes: уйти gives уйдя. Both clauses share the subject он, as is required. The imperfective уходя means 'as one leaves': уходя, гасите свет.

RU-C1-05-005.notes: сдать gives the past active participle сдавший = который сдал. It agrees with студент in the nominative.

RU-C1-05-006.notes: поднять gives the past passive participle поднятый, with -т-. It agrees with вопросы: поднятые. Verbs in -нять typically take -т-: принятый, занятый.

RU-C1-05-007.notes: стоять gives the present active participle стоящий = который стоит. стоящий also means 'worthwhile' as an adjective, from стоить.

RU-C1-05-008.notes: Relative чей agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: автор, чья книга. книга is feminine, so чья.

RU-C1-05-009.notes: Relative чей takes the case of its own clause: не помню имени, so the genitive чьего (имени). Speech prefers который: имени которого.

RU-C1-05-010.notes: каков is a short form of какой, used as a predicate in formal style: Каков результат? It agrees with результат.

RU-C1-06-001.notes: An impersonal verb + instrumental describes natural forces: дорогу замело снегом. There's no subject, so the verb is neuter.

RU-C1-06-002.notes: Крышу сорвало ветром: the roof is accusative, the wind instrumental, the verb neuter. English needs the wind as subject.

RU-C1-06-003.notes: Мне не верится is an impersonal -ся form: I can't quite believe. It's softer than я не верю. The past is мне не верилось.

RU-C1-06-004.notes: Ему не сидится на месте means he's restless and can't sit still. The impersonal -ся form is typical of inner states.

RU-C1-06-005.notes: Было решено uses the neuter short passive participle with no subject: it was decided. An infinitive follows.

RU-C1-06-006.notes: Мне везёт means 'I'm lucky', with the person in the dative. It's the same verb as везти (carry), used impersonally.

RU-C1-06-007.notes: тошнить is impersonal, with the person in the accusative: его тошнит. Most impersonal verbs use the dative instead.

RU-C1-07-001.notes: в случае если (in the event that) is a formal conditional. The noun form is в случае + genitive: в случае отмены.

RU-C1-07-002.notes: при условии, что means 'on condition that'. The comma goes before что. The noun phrase is при условии + genitive: при условии оплаты.

RU-C1-07-003.notes: если только не means 'unless': если только не будет дождя. Without только, the meaning is a plain negative condition.

RU-C1-07-004.notes: вряд ли means 'hardly, unlikely'. It's followed by a positive verb: вряд ли придёт, not вряд ли не придёт.

RU-C1-07-005.notes: Едва ли is a more formal synonym of вряд ли. Both express doubt about a positive statement. Едва on its own means 'barely': он едва успел.

RU-C1-07-006.notes: будто (as if, supposedly) signals that the speaker doubts the reported claim. With говорит, it means 'claims'.

RU-C1-07-007.notes: Раз (since, given that) introduces a known fact as a reason. It's colloquial and often begins the sentence.

RU-C1-07-008.notes: не столько…, сколько… means 'not so much… as…'. It corrects or refines a description. The adjectives after it are usually short forms.

RU-C1-07-009.notes: The generalised ты form describes anyone: тише едешь. Proverbs often use it. English uses 'you' the same way.

RU-C1-08-001.notes: Разве expresses doubt or surprise that something isn't so; Неужели expresses amazement at something hard to believe. Both start the question.

RU-C1-08-002.notes: всё-таки (all the same, after all) marks something that happened despite expectations. It's written with a hyphen.

RU-C1-08-003.notes: как раз means 'just, exactly': как раз вовремя. It also means 'the right size': как раз по размеру. In speech it also means 'that's exactly it': вот как раз!

RU-C1-08-004.notes: вот-вот means 'any moment now' and goes with the perfective future: вот-вот отправится. It's written with a hyphen. With a past form it means 'very nearly': вот-вот не упал.

RU-C1-08-005.notes: так и не + perfective past means something never happened in the end: так и не позвонил. It implies it was expected.

RU-C1-08-006.notes: Не хотите ли…? is a very polite offer. ли follows the verb, and чаю is a partitive genitive. The answer could be Да, с удовольствием.

RU-C1-08-007.notes: мол is a colloquial particle marking reported speech: he said, so to speak. It's set off by commas. It distances the speaker from the words, often with a hint of scepticism.

RU-C1-08-008.notes: якобы (allegedly) casts doubt on the reported reason. It's common in journalism. It implies the speaker doesn't believe the claim.

RU-C1-08-009.notes: дескать is an old-fashioned reported-speech particle, often ironic. It's rarer than мол and mostly found in literature. It is set off by commas.

RU-C1-09-001.notes: Collective numbers (двое, трое) are used with male people, children and plural-only nouns: двое детей. They take the genitive plural.

RU-C1-09-002.notes: Нас было трое means 'there were three of us'. Collective numbers are preferred with personal pronouns.

RU-C1-09-003.notes: сутки (24 hours) is plural-only, so it takes a collective number: двое суток. два суток is impossible.

RU-C1-09-004.notes: полтора (1.5) is used with masculine and neuter nouns and takes the genitive singular: полтора часа.

RU-C1-09-005.notes: полторы is used with feminine nouns: полторы тысячи. The oblique form is полутора for all genders. тысяча is feminine, which is why полторы is used.

RU-C1-09-006.notes: Putting the noun before the number makes it approximate: часа два (about two hours). The case doesn't change.

RU-C1-09-007.notes: Inversion gives approximation here too: лет пятьдесят (about fifty). The genitive лет still governs.

RU-C1-09-008.notes: сорок has the oblique form сорока in all cases except the accusative. около takes the genitive. девяносто and сто follow the same pattern: девяноста, ста.

RU-C1-09-009.notes: сто has the oblique form ста. более + genitive means 'more than'. The verb is usually neuter singular: пришло.

RU-C1-09-010.notes: девяносто has the oblique form девяноста. к + dative means 'by' an age. In speech, к девяноста годам is often shortened to к девяноста.

RU-C1-09-011.notes: Decimals are read as fractions: две целых три десятых (2.3). целых is genitive plural after две. The fraction agrees with the understood noun часть (part).

RU-C1-09-012.notes: четверть (quarter) is a feminine -ь noun, so the verb is feminine: прошла четверть часа. The noun is followed by the genitive: четверть часа.

RU-C1-09-013.notes: Distributive по + dative means 'each': по яблоку. With numbers above one it takes the accusative: по два яблока.
